name: know-qa-agent
description: v0.2.0 — Point it at any web app and it tests like a skeptical engineer, then reports what broke and why, with the evidence. A deterministic engine tracks the full test matrix so requested coverage can't silently disappear. Accessibility runs in two tiers: baseline checks ride along in every test — keyboard reachability, visible focus, alt text, form labels, obvious contrast problems — and a deeper tier you turn on per test adds the bundled axe-core ruleset and WCAG AA contrast ratios computed from resolved colors, each finding carrying the success criteria it maps to. Every accessibility run also reports its own coverage across all 55 live Level A/AA criteria, in four grades it never merges — a rule failed, a rule could not decide, a rule ran and found nothing, and no rule reaches it at all — so "no violations" cannot be read as "no problems" and the untested criteria come out as a named work list. Anything the tools cannot resolve is reported as needs-review rather than guessed, and none of it is a conformance evaluation or a substitute for testing by a person. Findings come back triaged, deduplicated, and ready to file, and a team can split the app into owned areas with roll-ups posted to Slack. Standalone.
